readback_body:
## Description
On mobile, a vertical finger drag inside the Nession terminal may fail to scroll content, particularly in full-screen / mouse-aware TUIs (Vim, Claude Code and similar). Ordinary shell local scrollback and TUI scrolling have different semantics and must both work.

## Reproduction
1. Open the current mobile App Terminal, attach to a session, produce more output than one screen, and swipe vertically to inspect history.
2. Enter a mouse-aware TUI or alternate-screen program and swipe to scroll its own view.
3. Compare against desktop wheel scrolling and App's top-level edge navigation.

**User-reported on 2026-11-03.** Browser reproduction on physical mobile remains pending.

## Investigation Status
Static inspection of `web/src/platform/terminal-runtime/capsule/occlusionScroll.ts` confirms that the touchmove callback immediately returns when `shouldScrollLocally()` is false. It is false when the TUI enables mouse tracking or uses alternate buffer. Thus no local scroll action and no synthetic wheel/mouse path is sent from this handler in those cases. This is a concrete missing event path consistent with the report, but not yet proof of the only runtime cause.

## Impact
Mobile cannot reliably review shell history or scroll an active TUI, undermining PC↔phone session continuity.

## Fix Direction
Preserve terminal mode ownership: local normal-buffer history scrolls xterm's local buffer; mouse-aware/alternate-screen TUI drags enter xterm's wheel path; horizontal selection/pager, taps, long-press arrow gesture (#2657), and multi-touch do not get claimed as scroll. Accumulate sub-cell drag deltas instead of treating every high-frequency move as one line.

## Location
`web/src/platform/terminal-runtime/capsule/occlusionScroll.ts`, `web/src/app/experiences/app/useSwipePager.ts`, xterm 5.5 input path.

### Success Criteria
- [ ] SC-01 Normal-buffer local history moves on a single-finger vertical swipe without changing the PTY or jumping many lines on tiny deltas.
- [ ] SC-02 Mouse-reporting/alternate-screen TUIs receive scroll input via xterm's existing mode semantics.
- [ ] SC-03 Horizontal selection, edge pager, quick tap, multitouch, and the separate planned long-press gesture (#2657) are not hijacked.
- [ ] SC-04 Mobile touch regression test verifies ownership across all three terminal modes.
